title: Follow the Bubbles: July 18, 2023
place: Sanak seeps, Aleutian margin off Alaska, ~2,100 m depth (Seascape Alaska 3, EX2304 Dive 04)
notes: A dense 'river' of methane gas bubbles races along under a rock overhang. It looks like silvery water flowing sideways or upside down, which is uncanny. 0-5.5 s: a sheet of bubbles fills the frame diagonally, with orange anemones at the left/top edges. 5.5-12.9 s: a nearly static close-up of the grey bubble curtain streaming under a rock ledge (top), with an anemone at the right edge. The bubble mass fills x~0.1-0.85, centre ~0.45. Best seconds 5.5-12.9. Note the source file is named 1920x1080 but is actually 1280x720; it was upscaled to 1920x1080. The cut is 12.9 s because of shot boundaries (39.24 s and 52.29 s in the source). No people, no logos or text (the title card, map graphics and end card are outside the window).
fact_en: The line of Sanak seeps emits a curtain of gas rising more than 1,500 meters (4,920 feet) above the seafloor; the dive explored them at 2,100 meters (6,900 feet) water depth.
